mainTopic: Is a man forbidden to all women after sending an agent to betroth an unnamed woman? רבי יוחנן's ruling and ריש לקיש's challenge from bird offerings (קינים)
overview: רבי יוחנן rules that if a man tells a שליח, 'Go betroth a woman for me' without naming her, he becomes forbidden to every woman in the world. We assume the שליח did his job, but the man does not know who his wife is, so any woman might be her close relative. ריש לקיש challenges this from a משנה about offering birds: when a consecrated bird flies away, we do not suspect every bird in the world of being the runaway. רבי יוחנן answers that a woman is fixed in her home, while a bird moves around, so with birds we follow the majority. Even if the woman was betrothed in the market, she goes back home, and a bird does not. רבא then limits the ruling: a woman with no relatives the שליח could have betrothed is permitted. This includes a woman whose relative was married when the שליח was sent and divorced later. The גמרא explains that a person sends a שליח only for women available at that moment. It then challenges this from a משנה about two people who each promise to pay for a נזיר's offerings, where the first seems to be able to pay for someone who was not yet a נזיר when he spoke. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: An unnamed betrothal forbids a man to all women
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a man who sends a שליח to betroth an unspecified woman becomes forbidden to all women, because the שליח surely did it but the man does not know who she is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man says, 'Go and betroth a woman for me' without saying which one, he is forbidden to all the women in the world. We presume that a שליח carries out his mission. Since the שליח did not tell him who she is, he does not know which woman was betrothed to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states רבי יוחנן's rule: after sending a שליח to betroth an unnamed woman, the man may not marry any woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ideas combine here. First, the חזקה that a שליח does what he was sent to do, so we treat the man as already married. Second, he does not know who his wife is, so any woman he marries might be her mother, sister or daughter, all of whom are forbidden to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Betroth for me (perform קידושין on my behalf)
A legal presumption we rely on
An agent carries out his assigned mission
He did not specify to him

steps.confusionAlert: He is not forbidden because he is married to every woman. He is forbidden because any woman might be a close relative of the one wife he does not know.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the claim that ריש לקיש attacks next: does an unknown item really make every similar item doubtful?

phrases.english: "Go out and betroth a woman for me," without specifying —
he is forbidden to all the women in the world.
There is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission,
and since he did not specify to him,
then he does not know
which one he betrothed for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who sends a שליח to betroth an unspecified woman is forbidden to all women, because the שליח is presumed to have done it and the identity of the wife is unknown.

steps.title: ריש לקיש quotes the משנה about a bird that flew away
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings a משנה: if one bird from an undesignated pair escapes or dies, the owner buys a new partner. If the pair was already designated, there is no fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש objected to רבי יוחנן from a משנה. If one bird from an undesignated pair of offering birds flew off into the open air, or flew in among the sin-offering birds that are left to die, or one of them died, the owner buys a partner for the remaining bird. But if the pair was already designated, there is no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש begins his challenge by quoting a משנה about offering birds. He is setting up the source; the actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'nest' is a pair of birds, one for an עולה and one for a חטאת. If the roles were not yet assigned, losing one bird is no problem: he buys another and assigns roles then. If the roles were already assigned, he does not know whether the bird that is left is the עולה or the חטאת, so it cannot be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: An unspecified pair of birds, not yet assigned as עולה or חטאת
Sin-offerings that are left to die
A pair whose roles were already assigned
Remedy, a way to fix the situation

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
An unspecified nest
phrases.notes: A pair of birds for an עולה and a חטאת, before anyone has decided which bird is which. Source: משנה קנים 2:1.

phrases.english: from which one of the fledglings flew away
into the open air of the world,
or flew in among the sin-offerings left to die,
or one of them died —
he takes a partner for the second one.
Whereas a specified nest —
it has no remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to attack רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that an unknown betrothed woman makes all women forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it gives the case of a lost bird, which is used in the next step to show that we do not suspect every similar item.

steps.title: Why not worry that every bird is the runaway?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש infers that everyone else's birds stay usable, and asks: by רבי יוחנן's logic, we should suspect every bird of being the lost one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But other people's nests in general are fit. Why? We should say about each and every bird, 'Maybe this is the one that flew away!'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש draws an inference from the משנה and turns it into a direct question against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only worries about the owner's own designated pair. It never forbids other people's birds, even though the runaway consecrated bird could be any bird in the world. If we do not suspect every bird, why should we suspect every woman of being related to the unknown wife?
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's challenge: the משנה about birds does not suspect every bird of being the lost one, so רבי יוחנן should not suspect every woman of being related to the unknown wife.
steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not arguing about the owner's own pair. He agrees that the specified pair has no fix. His point is about all the other birds in the world.

phrases.english: Whereas other nests in general
are fit.
But why?
Let us say about each and every one
perhaps this is the one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי לֵימָא כׇּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא דִּלְמָא הַאי נִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from step 2 to build the actual question against step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that every woman is forbidden because she might be related to the unknown wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה does not suspect every bird in the world of being the escaped consecrated bird. By the same logic, we should not suspect every woman of being a relative of the unknown betrothed woman.

steps.title: A woman stays put, a bird wanders
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש: his ruling is about a woman, who does not move around, while the bird case is about a prohibition that moves around.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am talking about a woman, who does not move around, and you are bringing me a prohibition that moves around?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's question from the birds. He says the bird case is not like his case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman lives in a fixed home, so the doubt about her is treated as an even 50/50 and we cannot simply follow the majority. A lost bird flies around, so we follow the majority of birds in the world, which are permitted. That is why other people's birds stay usable while every woman is forbidden to this man.

keyTerms.meaning: moves around, not fixed in one place
I am saying, I am talking about

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic difference between something fixed in place and something that moves around. That difference decides whether we can follow the majority when we are unsure.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is answering ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: I am speaking of a woman, who does not move around,
and you tell me about a prohibition that moves around?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the bird challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases: a fixed item compared with a moving item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird case shows we do not suspect every item of being the forbidden one.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is only true for things that move around. A woman, who is fixed in her home, is treated as an even doubt.

steps.title: But maybe she was found in the market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible comeback: the woman also 'moved', since the שליח may have found her in the market and betrothed her there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: here too she moves around, since we can say the שליח found her in the market and betrothed her there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a possible objection to רבי יוחנן's answer. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection says the woman was not fixed when she was betrothed, because it may have happened out in the street. If so, she should count as 'moving' just like the bird, and we should follow the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: let us say, it is possible that

phrases.english: And if you would say: here too, it moves around,
say he found her in the market and betrothed her,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible weakness in step 4's difference between the cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that a woman is fixed in place
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The betrothal may have happened in a public place, so the woman was moving around just like the bird.

steps.title: She goes home, a bird does not
steps.stepSummary: Even if she was betrothed in the market, a woman goes back to her home. A bird has no fixed place it returns to.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, she returns to her resting place. But a bird from a nest, does it return?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from step 5. A woman always comes back home, so she still counts as fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where she happened to be when she was betrothed does not matter. What matters is that her place is her home, and she returns there. A bird that flew off does not go back to any fixed spot, so it stays in the 'moving' category.

keyTerms.meaning: a pair of birds brought as an offering (literally 'nest')

steps.whatToRemember: A woman counts as fixed because she always returns home. A bird does not, so the bird case cannot be used against רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: there, she returns to her resting place,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the woman's case, and her 'resting place' is her home.

phrases.english: regarding a nest, does it return?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies what makes something count as fixed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since she may have been betrothed in the market, the woman should count as moving.
steps.terutzMaskana: She returns home, so she is still fixed. A bird never returns.

steps.title: When רבי יוחנן agrees the woman is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי יוחנן agrees: a woman with no relatives the שליח could have betrothed is permitted. This includes a woman whose sister was married at the time and divorced later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוחנן agrees about a woman who has no daughter, no daughter's daughter, no son's daughter, no mother, no mother's mother, and no sister. Even if she had a sister who was later divorced, this woman is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a limit to רבי יוחנן's ruling. A woman with no relatives the שליח could have betrothed is permitted to the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is only forbidden to a woman because the שליח might have betrothed one of her close relatives. If she has no such relatives, there is nothing to worry about. רבא adds that a sister who was married at the time and divorced later does not create a problem either.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן's ruling forbids the man to every woman with no exceptions. It only applies where the שליח could have betrothed one of her close relatives.

phrases.english: Rava said: And Rabbi Yochanan agrees
regarding a woman who has no daughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בַּת בַּת, וְלֹא בַּת בֵּן,
phrases.english: nor a daughter's daughter, nor a son's daughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֵם, וְלֹא אֵם אֵם, וְלֹא אָחוֹת.
phrases.english: nor a mother, nor a mother's mother, nor a sister.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ אָחוֹת
phrases.english: And even though she had a sister
phrases.notes: The sister was married when the שליח was sent.

phrases.english: who was divorced after this,
that this one is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from defending the ruling to setting its limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with no relatives the שליח could have betrothed is permitted, even if a sister was married then and divorced later.

steps.title: A שליח is only sent for women available now
steps.stepSummary: The reason: when the man sent the שליח, those relatives were married. A person only sends a שליח for something that is available at that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because at the time he told the שליח, those relatives were married to men. When a person sends a שליח, it is for something in front of him. For something not in front of him, he does not send a שליח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבא's rule about the sister who was divorced later. The man never sent the שליח to betroth women who were married at that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח can only do what he was sent to do. The man was thinking only of women who were available when he spoke. So even if the שליח betrothed the sister after her divorce, that betrothal would not work, and her sister stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: stands before him, is available now

steps.whatToRemember: A שליח is only sent for what is available at the moment he is sent. Women who were married then were never part of his job.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about שליחות. A person's appointment of a שליח covers only things that could happen at that time.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because at that time when he told him,
they were married to men.
When one appoints an agent,
it is for a matter that stands before him.
For a matter that does not stand before him,
he does not appoint an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבא's rule about the sister who was divorced later.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is a woman permitted if her sister was divorced after the שליח was sent?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שליח is only appointed for women available at that moment, and the sister was married then.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה of two people who promise to pay for each other's nazirite offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: one person says he is a נזיר and will pay for another נזיר's shaving offerings. His friend says the same. If they are smart, they pay for each other's offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: someone said, 'I am a נזיר, and I take upon myself to pay for the shaving of a נזיר.' His friend heard and said, 'Me too, and I take upon myself to pay for the shaving of a נזיר.' If they are smart, they pay for each other. If not, they pay for other נזירים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה to set up a challenge. The challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets each person keep his promise by paying for the other's offerings. That means the first person's promise can count toward someone who only became a נזיר after he spoke. This will clash with the rule from step 8 that a person only has in mind what is available at that moment.

keyTerms.meaning: To pay for the offerings a נזיר brings when he shaves at the end of his נזירות

phrases.english: We learned: 'I am hereby a nazirite
and it is upon me to shave a nazirite,'
phrases.notes: 'To shave a נזיר' means paying for the offerings he must bring when he shaves at the end of his נזירות.

phrases.english: and his friend heard and said:
'And I, and it is upon me to shave a nazirite,'
phrases.notes: 'And I' means: I am also a נזיר, just like you.

phrases.english: if they are clever
they shave each other,
phrases.notes: Each one pays for the other's offerings. That way each keeps his promise, and neither pays for a stranger.

phrases.english: and if not,
they shave other nazirites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה that will be used to challenge the reasoning of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 8 that a person only has in mind what is available at that moment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup: it shows that the first person's promise can be kept through someone who was not yet a נזיר when he spoke.

steps.title: The first person could not have meant the second nazirite
steps.stepSummary: The second person can pay for the first, because the first was already a נזיר. But when the first person made his promise, the second was not yet a נזיר. So how can the first pay for the second?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the second person, since the first was already a נזיר in front of him. But the first person: was the second one already a נזיר in front of him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks its challenge. Based on the משנה, it questions the rule that a person only has in mind what is available at that moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the second person spoke, the first was already a נזיר, so he could have meant him. When the first person spoke, the second was not yet a נזיר. By the rule of step 8, the first could not have meant him. Yet the משנה lets him keep his promise by paying for the second.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for this part)
The last one, the second person
Before him, already there when he spoke

steps.confusionAlert: The question is only about the first person. The second person's case is fine, because the first was already a נזיר when he spoke.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this question stands, it weakens the reason the גמרא gave in step 8 for רבא's rule about the sister who was divorced later.

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding the last one:
there is the first one before him.
phrases.notes: 'Before him' means the first person was already a נזיר when the second made his promise.

phrases.english: But the first one:
is the last one before him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in step 9 to challenge the reasoning of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 8 that a person only sends or commits for what is available at that moment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets the first person keep his promise by paying for someone who was not yet a נזיר when he spoke. So people can commit to something that is not yet available.
